subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we say a switch 'controls' a circuit but is not a 'source' of electricity?
prompt_hi: Hum kyon kehte hain ki switch circuit ko 'control' karta hai par bijli ka 'source' nahi hai?
answer: Because the cell provides the energy that drives the current; the switch only opens or closes the path, deciding whether current can flow.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two circuit diagrams each have a cell and a bulb. In diagram A the switch symbol shows a gap; in diagram B it shows no gap. In which will the bulb glow, and why?
prompt_hi: Do circuit diagram mein cell aur bulb hain. Diagram A mein switch symbol mein gap hai; diagram B mein gap nahi hai. Kismein bulb jalega, aur kyon?
answer: In B, because the closed switch completes the circuit; in A the switch is open, so the circuit is broken.

subject: science
prompt_en: Turn this description into a circuit diagram: 'A battery of three cells, a switch and two bulbs, all in one loop.' Then say what each symbol in your drawing looks like.
prompt_hi: Is description ko circuit diagram mein badlo: 'Teen cell ki battery, ek switch aur do bulb, sab ek hi loop mein.' Phir batao tumhare drawing ka har symbol kaisa dikhta hai.
answer: Three cell symbols in a row, with the long line of each next to the short line of the next; a switch symbol; two bulb symbols (circles with crosses); all joined by straight lines into one closed loop.

subject: science
prompt_en: In your room, a switch on the switchboard controls the fan. Where is the circuit, and what does the switch do when you turn it OFF?
prompt_hi: Tumhare kamre mein switchboard ka ek switch pankha chalata hai. Circuit kahaan hai, aur switch OFF karne pe wo kya karta hai?
answer: Wires inside the walls connect the supply to the fan and back, forming a circuit; turning the switch OFF opens the circuit, so current stops and the fan stops. (Never open a switchboard yourself.)

subject: science
prompt_en: A refrigerator's light turns on when you open the door and off when you close it. What device is hidden there, and how does it work?
prompt_hi: Fridge ki light darwaza kholne pe jalti hai aur band karne pe bujh jaati hai. Wahaan kaunsa device chhupa hai, aur wo kaise kaam karta hai?
answer: A small push switch. When the door is closed it presses the switch and opens (breaks) the light's circuit; when the door opens, the switch is released and the circuit closes, so the light glows.

subject: science
prompt_en: Kiran drew a cell with the short thick line labelled '+' and the long thin line labelled '−'. What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Kiran ne cell ka symbol banaya jismein chhoti moti line pe '+' aur lambi patli line pe '−' likha. Galti kya hai?
answer: The labels are swapped: the long thin line is positive and the short thick line is negative.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend why scientists use circuit diagrams with symbols instead of drawing real-looking pictures of cells and bulbs.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki scientists cell aur bulb ki asli jaisi picture banaane ki bajaye symbols wale circuit diagram kyon use karte hain.
answer: Symbols are quick to draw, simple and standard everywhere, so anyone can read the diagram and build exactly the same circuit.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what does the longer line in a cell symbol stand for?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: cell ke symbol mein lambi line kis cheez ko dikhati hai?
answer: The positive terminal.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these into conductors and insulators: steel spoon, plastic scale, iron key, rubber band, aluminium foil, wooden ice-cream stick.
prompt_hi: Inhe conductor aur insulator mein baanto: steel ka chammach, plastic ka scale, lohe ki chaabi, rubber band, aluminium foil, lakdi ki ice-cream stick.
answer: Conductors: steel spoon, iron key, aluminium foil. Insulators: plastic scale, rubber band, wooden ice-cream stick.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict, then check with your cell-and-bulb tester: will a steel hairpin make the bulb glow? A plastic button? A one-rupee coin?
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo, phir apne cell-bulb tester se check karo: kya steel ka hairpin bulb jalaayega? Plastic ka button? Ek rupaye ka sikka?
answer: The hairpin and the coin make it glow because they are metals; the plastic button does not, because plastic is an insulator.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you touch the tester's two wire ends to the two ends of a lead from a mechanical pencil, will the bulb glow?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar tester ke dono taar ke sire mechanical pencil ki lead ke dono siron se chhuaao, toh kya bulb jalega?
answer: Yes, it conducts: graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity. The bulb may glow dimly; an LED tester shows it more clearly.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your tester uses an LED instead of a torch bulb, because an LED lights up with a much smaller current. Dip its two wire ends in a glass of tap water, not touching each other. Predict what happens. Then predict what happens after you stir in two spoons of salt.
prompt_hi: Tumhare tester mein torch bulb ki jagah LED hai, kyonki LED bahut kam current mein bhi jal jaata hai. Iske dono taar nal ke paani ke glass mein daalo, ek doosre ko chhue bina. Guess karo kya hoga. Phir do chammach namak ghol ke guess karo kya hoga.
answer: In tap water the LED stays dark or glows very faintly; after salt is dissolved it glows clearly, because salt water conducts much better. Either way, water can conduct, which is why water and mains electricity are dangerous together.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are electric wires made of copper inside and covered with plastic outside?
prompt_hi: Bijli ke taar andar se copper ke aur bahar se plastic se dhake kyon hote hain?
answer: Copper is a good conductor and carries current easily; plastic is an insulator that keeps the current inside the wire and protects us from shocks.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves and rubber-soled shoes while working?
prompt_hi: Electrician kaam karte waqt rubber ke gloves aur rubber sole wale joote kyon pehente hain?
answer: Rubber is an insulator; it blocks current from passing through their body to the ground, protecting them from electric shock.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two screwdrivers: one with a plastic handle, one made all of metal. Which is safer for an electrician, and why?
prompt_hi: Do screwdriver: ek plastic handle wala, ek poora metal ka. Electrician ke liye kaunsa zyada safe hai, aur kyon?
answer: The one with the plastic handle, because plastic is an insulator and stops current from reaching the hand; an all-metal one would conduct it.

subject: science
prompt_en: During a storm, an electric wire has fallen on a wet road near your school. Why should you stay far away and tell an adult, even if it looks harmless?
prompt_hi: Toofan ke dauraan school ke paas geeli sadak pe bijli ka taar gir gaya hai. Wo bekaar dikhe phir bhi tumhe door kyon rehna chahiye aur kisi bade ko kyon batana chahiye?
answer: The wire may still be live; current can pass through wet ground and water and through your body, giving a deadly shock. Keep away and tell an adult, who can call the electricity department.

subject: science
prompt_en: Cooking pans in Indian kitchens have metal bodies but often wooden or plastic handles. Is this the same idea as electric wires? Explain.
prompt_hi: Indian kitchen ke bartan metal ke hote hain par handle aksar lakdi ya plastic ke. Kya ye bijli ke taar wala hi idea hai? Samjhao.
answer: It is a similar idea, but for heat: metal conducts heat well to cook the food, while wood and plastic are poor conductors of heat, so the handle stays cool. Many good conductors of electricity, like metals, are also good conductors of heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sameer tested tap water with a torch-bulb tester, saw no glow, and wrote: 'Water is an insulator, so it's fine to use a hair dryer in the bathroom with wet hands.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Sameer ne nal ke paani ko torch-bulb tester se test kiya, bulb nahi jala, aur likha: 'Paani insulator hai, toh geele haathon se bathroom mein hair dryer chalaana theek hai.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Tap water conducts weakly: too little current for a torch bulb with one cell, but mains voltage can push a dangerous current through water and wet skin. Never use electrical appliances with wet hands.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a two-column chart from these test results, 'bulb glowed' and 'bulb did not glow': iron nail, rubber eraser, aluminium foil, glass bangle, steel spoon, paper, pencil lead. Then label the columns with the right science words.
prompt_hi: In test results se do column ka chart banao, 'bulb jala' aur 'bulb nahi jala': lohe ki keel, rubber eraser, aluminium foil, kaanch ki choodi, steel ka chammach, kaagaz, pencil lead. Phir columns pe sahi science ke shabd likho.
answer: Bulb glowed (conductors): iron nail, aluminium foil, steel spoon, pencil lead. Bulb did not glow (insulators): rubber eraser, glass bangle, paper.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your grandmother why she should dry her hands before switching on the mixer-grinder.
prompt_hi: Apni daadi ya naani ko samjhao ki mixer-grinder ka switch on karne se pehle haath kyon sukhaane chahiye.
answer: Water on the hands can conduct electricity, so if current leaks it could pass through the wet skin and body and give a shock; dry hands and the switch's plastic cover keep her safe.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one non-metal that conducts electricity.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi non-metal ka naam batao jo bijli conduct karti hai.
answer: Graphite (pencil lead).

subject: science
prompt_en: Which property lets copper be drawn into thin wires, and which property makes a temple bell ring?
prompt_hi: Kaunsi property ki wajah se copper ko patle taar mein kheencha ja sakta hai, aur kaunsi property mandir ki ghanti ko bajaati hai?
answer: Ductility lets copper be drawn into wires; sonority makes a metal bell ring.

subject: science
prompt_en: Gently tap a steel glass, then a wooden block and a plastic box, with a steel spoon. Predict which will ring.
prompt_hi: Ek steel ke glass, phir ek lakdi ke tukde aur plastic ke dibbe ko steel ke chammach se halke se thapthapaao. Guess karo kaun bajega, yaani kaun ki aawaaz goonjegi?
answer: The steel glass rings because metals are sonorous; the wooden block and plastic box give only a dull thud.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you bring a fridge magnet near an iron nail, a ball of aluminium foil, a copper wire and a brass key, which ones will it pull?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar fridge wala magnet lohe ki keel, aluminium foil ki goli, copper ke taar aur peetal ki chaabi ke paas laao, toh wo kis-kisko kheenchega?
answer: Only the iron nail. Aluminium, copper and brass are metals too, but magnets attract only iron, nickel, cobalt and things made with them.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you gently bend a piece of pencil lead (graphite) and a piece of aluminium wire, which one bends and which one snaps?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar pencil ki lead (graphite) ka tukda aur aluminium ke taar ka tukda halke se modo, toh kaun mud jaayega aur kaun toot jaayega?
answer: The aluminium wire bends because metals are ductile and malleable; the graphite snaps because non-metals are brittle.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are cooking vessels like a kadhai or pateela usually made of iron, steel or aluminium?
prompt_hi: Kadhai ya pateela jaise khaana banane ke bartan aksar lohe, steel ya aluminium ke kyon bante hain?
answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so heat passes quickly from the flame to the food; they are also strong and can be shaped because they are malleable.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare graphite and diamond. Both are made only of carbon. How are they different, and which one conducts electricity?
prompt_hi: Graphite aur diamond ki tulna karo. Dono sirf carbon se bane hain. Ye alag kaise hain, aur inmein se kaun bijli conduct karta hai?
answer: Graphite is soft, dark grey and slippery and conducts electricity (it is used in pencils); diamond is extremely hard and transparent and does not conduct electricity.

subject: science
prompt_en: Silver varq on mithai is a sheet thinner than paper. Which property of silver makes this possible?
prompt_hi: Mithai pe lagne wala chaandi ka varq kaagaz se bhi patla hota hai. Chaandi ki kaunsi property se ye mumkin hai?
answer: Malleability: silver can be beaten into extremely thin sheets.

subject: science
prompt_en: You must choose a material for the bells on a dancer's ghungroo. Would you pick plastic or brass? Explain using properties.
prompt_hi: Tumhe ek dancer ke ghungroo ki ghantiyon ke liye material chunna hai. Plastic chunoge ya peetal? Properties use karke samjhao.
answer: Brass, a metal alloy, because metals are sonorous and make a ringing sound when struck; plastic would only click dully.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ritu writes: 'All metals are hard and solid, and none can be cut with a knife.' Correct her.
prompt_hi: Ritu likhti hai: 'Saare metals sakht aur thos hote hain, aur kisi ko chaaku se nahi kaat sakte.' Use sahi karo.
answer: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature, and sodium and potassium are metals soft enough to be cut with a knife (they react with air and water, so they are kept under kerosene and never handled at home).

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a table with rows for lustre, malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction, and columns for copper and sulphur. Fill it in and say what pattern you see.
prompt_hi: Ek table banao jismein rows ho chamak, malleability, ductility, sonority aur conduction, aur columns ho copper aur sulphur. Bharo aur batao kya pattern dikhta hai.
answer: Copper: lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductor. Sulphur: dull yellow, brittle, not ductile, not sonorous, poor conductor. Pattern: metals and non-metals have opposite properties.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend how you could tell whether an unknown shiny solid is a metal, using three safe tests. Why is shine alone not enough?
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki kisi anjaan chamakdaar thos cheez ko metal hai ya nahi, 3 safe tests se kaise pata karoge. Sirf chamak kaafi kyon nahi hai?
answer: Tap it to hear if it rings (sonority); try bending a thin piece to see if it bends or crumbles (malleable or brittle); put it in a cell-and-bulb tester to see if it conducts. Shine is not enough because some non-metals, like iodine, are shiny too.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is ductility? Give one example.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ductility kya hai? Ek example do.
answer: Ductility is the property of being drawn into thin wires, for example copper or aluminium wires.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three ways to stop an iron gate from rusting.
prompt_hi: Lohe ke gate ko jung se bachaane ke 3 tareeke batao.
answer: Paint it; apply oil or grease; galvanise it with a coating of zinc; keep it dry.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ask an adult for three iron nails. Nail A goes into a closed, dry plastic box with a few packets of the silica gel that come in new shoe boxes (do not open or eat them) to soak up moisture. Nail B goes half into water in an open cup. Nail C goes into water that an adult has boiled and cooled, with a thin layer of cooking oil poured on top. Predict which nail will rust in a week.
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se 3 lohe ki keel maango. Keel A ko sukhe band plastic ke dibbe mein rakho, saath mein naye joote ke dibbe wale silica gel ke kuch packet daalo (unhe kholna ya khaana nahi) jo nami sokh lete hain. Keel B ko khule cup ke paani mein aadha daalo. Keel C ko us paani mein daalo jise kisi bade ne ubaal ke thanda kiya ho, aur upar se khaane ke tel ki patli parat daal do. Guess karo kaunsi keel ek hafte mein jung khaayegi.
answer: Nail B rusts the most because it has both air and water. Nail A has air but the silica gel keeps the air almost free of moisture, and nail C has water but almost no air (boiling drove the dissolved air out and the oil keeps it from coming back), so A and C stay almost rust-free.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if an iron nail rusts completely and you collect every bit of the rust, will the rust weigh more than, less than or the same as the original nail?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar ek lohe ki keel poori tarah jung kha jaaye aur tum saara jung ikattha kar lo, toh jung ka wazan original keel se zyada hoga, kam hoga ya barabar?
answer: More, because oxygen and water from the air have combined with the iron to make the rust.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two identical iron bicycles are left outside: one in Mumbai near the sea, one in dry Jaipur. Predict which rusts faster, and why.
prompt_hi: Do bilkul ek jaisi lohe ki cycle bahar chhodi gayi: ek Mumbai mein samudra ke paas, ek sukhe Jaipur mein. Guess karo kaunsi jaldi jung khaayegi, aur kyon?
answer: The one in Mumbai, because the air near the sea is humid and salty, and moisture and salt speed up rusting.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does painting an iron grill stop it from rusting, and why does rust start again where the paint gets scratched?
prompt_hi: Lohe ki grill pe paint karne se jung kyon nahi lagta, aur jahaan paint chhil jaata hai wahaan phir se jung kyon lagne lagta hai?
answer: Paint keeps air and water away from the iron; where it is scratched, the iron is exposed to air and moisture again and starts to rust.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare an old copper vessel and an old iron kadhai left in a damp storeroom for months. What will each look like?
prompt_hi: Ek purana copper ka bartan aur ek purani lohe ki kadhai mahino tak nam store room mein rakhe gaye. Dono kaise dikhenge?
answer: The copper vessel gets a green coating; the iron kadhai gets reddish-brown, flaky rust.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are iron buckets and water pipes often coated with zinc, which is called galvanising?
prompt_hi: Lohe ki baaltiyon aur paani ke pipe pe aksar zinc ki parat kyon chadhaayi jaati hai, jise galvanising kehte hain?
answer: The zinc coating keeps air and water away from the iron so it does not rust; even if scratched, the zinc still protects the iron.
